title: Hash Maps and Postings Lists: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Hash Maps and Postings Lists: Visual Guide

1. From Cost To Structure | a dictionary-size slider pricing lesson 01's linear scan, binary search and hash probe side by side, with the two lists that bridge that cost model into this lesson's structures | an inverted index needs two different structures, a dictionary for point lookup and a postings representation for ordered growth, and lesson 01's costs only decide anything once you name the operation

2. The Load Factor Dial | 750,000 terms held fixed while the bucket array M is dragged from 10,000 to 4,000,000, showing alpha, expected entries examined and the bucket memory | a hash lookup is expected O(1+alpha) and not O(1), so the same line of code examines 1.75 entries at alpha 0.75 and dozens at alpha 75, which is why tables resize geometrically

3. Chained Or Probed | keys 42, 18 and 50 inserted one at a time into an eight-bucket table, toggled between separate chaining and linear probing, with the comparison count for a missing key | collisions are structural rather than exceptional, chaining scans a bucket while probing walks consecutive slots until an empty one proves absence, and probing needs alpha below 1

4. Nodes Or Bytes | five postings operations tapped against a packed array and linked nodes, with a length slider showing 4 MB versus 16 MB at one million document IDs | append ties, everything else favours contiguous bytes, and the famous constant-time linked insertion assumes a predecessor pointer that costs O(n) to find

5. Order As Contract | five queries run against a hashed and a sorted one-million-term dictionary, with a slider for how many terms match | hashing answers get(key) and nothing ordered, while a sorted structure answers lower_bound, prefix, range and ordered merge in O(log n + k), so list the required operations before choosing
